```{r setup, include=FALSE}
.libPaths(c("/project/gilad/geena/Rlibs/R-4.4.1", .libPaths()))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5)
library(mashr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(tibble)
library(pheatmap)
library(RColorBrewer)

results_root <- "/project/gilad/geena/publication_clean/results/treatment"
mash_root <- file.path(results_root, "dreamlet_mash")

drugs <- c("Ale", "Bri", "Cer", "Cri", "Lor")
lfsr_cut <- 0.05
```

## Context

Diagnostic overview of the per-drug mash outputs (produced by `02_run_mash.R`).
Two things per drug: (1) how many DE genes per cell type, and (2) how the
breadth (K = number of cell types where the gene is DE) is distributed. Both
are useful sanity checks before writing supp tables or figures downstream --
none of the CSVs written here are consumed by other scripts in this repo,
so this notebook is safe to skip if the mash outputs already look right.

## Section 1 — Load and long-format the mash results

Wide matrices (14,918 genes x 30 cell types per drug) get pivoted to a long
tibble with one row per (drug, cell type, gene). NA cells (untestable in
the dreamlet fit) are dropped. `is_de = lfsr < 0.05`; `direction = sign(PM)`
on the DE subset.

```{r load-long}
load_wide_matrix <- function(drug, filename) {
  f <- file.path(mash_root, paste0("by_drug_", drug), filename)
  df <- read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
  # First column is the unnamed row-name column from write.csv; rename to gene.
  names(df)[1] <- "gene"
  df
}

pivot_mash <- function(drug) {
  lfsr <- load_wide_matrix(drug, "mash_lfsr.csv") %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "lfsr")
  pm <- load_wide_matrix(drug, "mash_pm.csv") %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "PM")
  lfc <- load_wide_matrix(drug, "logFC_original.csv") %>%
    pivot_longer(-gene, names_to = "cell_type", values_to = "logFC_original")
  lfsr %>%
    inner_join(pm, by = c("gene", "cell_type")) %>%
    inner_join(lfc, by = c("gene", "cell_type")) %>%
    mutate(drug = drug)
}

de_long <- map_dfr(drugs, pivot_mash) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lfsr)) %>%
  mutate(is_de = lfsr < lfsr_cut,
         direction = ifelse(is_de, sign(PM), NA_real_))

cat("de_long:", nrow(de_long),
    "rows (drug x cell_type x gene, NA cells dropped)\n")
```

## Section 2 — Per-CT DE counts (per drug)

Post-mash DE counts per cell type: how many DE genes recur in each cell type
for each drug, and how the up/down split falls.

```{r per-ct}
per_ct <- de_long %>%
  group_by(drug, cell_type) %>%
  summarize(
    n_de = sum(is_de),
    n_up = sum(is_de & direction > 0),
    n_down = sum(is_de & direction < 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

per_ct_wide <- per_ct %>%
  select(drug, cell_type, n_de) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = n_de, values_fill = 0L) %>%
  arrange(cell_type)
per_ct_wide
```

### Heatmap of n_de across cell type x drug

```{r per-ct-heatmap, fig.width=8, fig.height=9}
mat <- per_ct %>%
  select(drug, cell_type, n_de) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = n_de, values_fill = 0L) %>%
  column_to_rownames("cell_type") %>%
  as.matrix()
mat <- mat[, drugs]

pheatmap(mat,
         color = colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "YlOrRd"))(50),
         cluster_cols = FALSE, cluster_rows = TRUE,
         display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%d",
         fontsize_number = 7, fontsize_row = 8, fontsize_col = 10,
         main = "n DE genes (lfsr<0.05) per cell type x drug",
         border_color = "white")
```

## Section 3 — Breadth distribution (per drug)

For each (drug, gene), breadth K = number of cell types where the gene is DE.
mash is conservative on sharing so the tails of this distribution (K=1
cell-type-specific, K=30 all-shared) are reliable characterizations of how
each drug's DE signal is spread across cell types.

```{r breadth}
breadth <- de_long %>%
  group_by(drug, gene) %>%
  summarize(n_ct_tested = n(),
            K = sum(is_de),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(K >= 1)

classify_breadth <- function(K) {
  case_when(
    K == 1 ~ "CT-specific (K=1)",
    K <= 4 ~ "narrow-shared (2-4)",
    K <= 14 ~ "moderate-shared (5-14)",
    K <= 29 ~ "broadly-shared (15-29)",
    K == 30 ~ "all_shared (30)",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

class_order <- c("CT-specific (K=1)", "narrow-shared (2-4)",
                 "moderate-shared (5-14)", "broadly-shared (15-29)",
                 "all_shared (30)")
breadth <- breadth %>%
  mutate(class = factor(classify_breadth(K), levels = class_order))

breadth_table <- breadth %>%
  count(drug, class, name = "n_genes") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = drug, values_from = n_genes, values_fill = 0L) %>%
  arrange(class)
breadth_table
```

### Stacked bar of breadth classes

```{r breadth-bar, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
ggplot(breadth %>% count(drug, class, name = "n_genes"),
       aes(x = drug, y = n_genes, fill = class)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral", direction = -1) +
  labs(x = "Drug", y = "n genes DE in >=1 cell type",
       title = "Breadth composition of DE gene sets per drug",
       fill = "breadth class") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
```

### Full breadth distribution (K = 1 to 30 cell types)

```{r breadth-hist, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
ggplot(breadth, aes(x = K)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, boundary = 0.5, fill = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~ drug, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30)) +
  labs(x = "K = n cell types where gene is DE",
       y = "n genes",
       title = "Breadth K distribution per drug") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```
